criterion_notes.c1: Touches on urban drinking water and sewerage service access in Peru by summarizing national and utility-level (EPS) coverage gaps, hours of continuity, pressure, and average tariffs alongside utility operational metrics.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, the paper arguably touches on administrative, institutional, and regulatory topics (utility management of the 51 urban EPS, customer complaint procedures, metering/billing rules, average tariffs, and Obras por Impuestos/PPP investment mechanisms), although even under the plain reading the overall paper is still excluded because it lacks empirical analysis (c3) and an identifiable exposure-outcome design (c5). Under the active narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, c2 is 'no': the paper is an unanalysed macro-governance and general utility operations management overview (focusing on pipe aging, water losses, tree roots, salaries, and aggregate operational/commercial complaint totals as a general management indicator) and does not empirically examine how any specific legal or administrative rule governs household or community service access.
criterion_notes.c3: Fails c3 (exclude as E05). Although boilerplate text labels the study 'básica, enfoque cuantitativo, diseño no experimental y nivel descriptivo' using 'técnica documental', it contains no primary data, no specified dataset or sampling frame, no empirical or qualitative methodology, and no systematic synthesis; it is a narrative sector/policy overview pasting isolated secondary summary statistics from SUNASS benchmarking reports and press releases alongside operations-management textbook commentary.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports secondary aggregate indicators relevant to access, continuity, and affordability from SUNASS reports (e.g., 3.3 million Peruvians without public drinking water network and 6.4 million without sewerage connections; urban coverage of 92.5% in drinking water and 85.9% in sewerage; continuity hours in selected EPS; average tariff of S/ 2.941/m3), though these are presented only as descriptive background rather than outcomes linked to an analyzed exposure.
criterion_notes.c5: Fails c5. While the urban utility sector (50 municipal EPS plus SEDAPAL) is described at a macro level, no analytical exposure-outcome relationship or empirical study design is identifiable; the nominal focal variable ('proceso de reclamaciones') is never operationalized or linked to service access or management improvement outcomes beyond reporting a single national count of 443,673 complaints in 2022 and an anecdotal remark that ~10% of users complain annually.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with an English abstract; per Criterion 10, direct reading/translation from the provided Spanish full text is feasible, though the paper is excluded on methodological and scope grounds.

evidence_quotes.quote: la Superintendencia Nacional de Servicios de Saneamiento informó que actualmente 3.3 millones de peruanos no cuentan con una red pública de agua potable y 6.4 millones no tienen conexiones de alcantarillado.
Se realizó un análisis de teorías, precedentes históricos sobre la administración de redes de agua y alcantarillado, siendo este tema elegido por la realidad que vivimos.

El objetivo de la investigación fue analizar el proceso de reclamaciones como indicador de mejora en la gestión del sector saneamiento en el Perú. Las técnicas que se utilizaron fue la recopilación de datos, el análisis documental y la contrastación de la variable con la realidad de contexto (Cieza, 2023).
La figura 2 evidencia que se alcanzó un nivel máximo de 92.5% en el año 2017 en agua potable y 85.9% en alcantarillado.

aproximadamente el 10% de los usuarios reclama al menos una vez al año a pesar del procedimiento tedioso de tener que ir varias veces a las oficinas de las EPS, el tiempo que les demanda hacer colas y esperar su atención

raw_response.exposure: Nominally the customer complaints process (proceso de reclamaciones) and general urban sanitation utility management in Peru, though no exposure is empirically operationalized or analyzed against service access
raw_response.outcome: Secondary descriptive sector indicators from SUNASS reports (urban drinking water and sewerage coverage, continuity, pressure, water losses, micrometering, average tariffs, pipe breaks, and total registered customer complaints)
raw_response.population_and_sample: Urban water and sanitation sector in Peru (51 urban utilities: 50 municipal Entidades Prestadoras de Servicios de Saneamiento [EPS] and state-owned SEDAPAL)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E05 (No empirical evidence). Despite boilerplate descriptive/documentary labeling, this Spanish-language article is a narrative policy and operations-management overview of Peru's urban sanitation utilities (EPS) that summarizes isolated secondary headline statistics from SUNASS reports and press releases alongside management textbook commentary, without primary data, an identifiable dataset, or any empirical method (quantitative, qualitative, or systematic synthesis). It also fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2 (focusing on general utility operational management and aggregate customer complaint counts rather than a rule-type mechanism governing service access) and Criterion 5 (no identifiable analytical exposure-outcome relationship), so it would likewise be excluded under the plain wording of Criterion 2.
raw_response.study_design: Narrative documentary sector overview (self-described as basic, quantitative, non-experimental descriptive documentary review)
